prompt.context: Our client is one of the top three beverage manufacturers in the U.S. They are thinking of launching a new flavored non-sparkling water product. The company is a vertically integrated beverage manufacturer that makes the drinks, has five bottling plants, and owns their own distribution channels.
prompt.question: They have asked us to determine whether or not they should launch the new product, how to do it, and what the marketing strategy should be.

clarifying_info.q: What is the size of the entire flavored water market?
clarifying_info.a: There are 8 million gallons of water sold in the entire flavored water market per year.

clarifying_info.q: How is the flavored water market broken down by category?
clarifying_info.a: Sparkling water is 90% of the market; non-sparkling water is 10% of the market.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the current competitors in the non-sparkling water segment and what are their market shares?
clarifying_info.a: Two main competitors: Easy Drink (18% share) and O2 (12% share); Others make up 70%.

clarifying_info.q: What bottle size does the market use and what does our client plan to use?
clarifying_info.a: All drinks in the flavored non-sparkling water market are packaged in 16 oz bottles, and our client plans to do the same.

clarifying_info.q: How many ounces are in a gallon?
clarifying_info.a: There are 64 ounces in a gallon.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average price per bottle?
clarifying_info.a: Drinks are priced, on average, at $1 per bottle.

clarifying_info.q: What is the variable cost per bottle?
clarifying_info.a: Variable cost per bottle of flavored non-sparkling water is 90 cents.

clarifying_info.q: What are the start-up and launch costs?
clarifying_info.a: Start-up launch costs, including all initial R&D and marketing costs, are $400,000.

clarifying_info.q: How are the main competitors positioning their products?
clarifying_info.a: Provide the customer survey chart (Exhibit on p083) showing respondents' preferred beverage type by brand.

exhibits.title: Flavored Water Market by Category and by Product
exhibits.shows: Two pie charts: one showing the split of the overall flavored water market between sparkling and non-sparkling categories; one showing the split of the flavored non-sparkling water market among specific products.

exhibits.title: Respondents' Preferred Beverage Type
exhibits.shows: A chart from a recent customer survey showing how respondents prefer to categorize or use the main competing brands and 'other' products (e.g., sports drink, leisure beverage, etc.).
exhibits.data: Breakdown of preferred beverage type by brand/category as reported by survey respondents; exact percentages visible in chart.

framework: Market sizing: quantify the non-sparkling water market in bottles sold and revenue
Competitive landscape: identify key players, market share concentration, and entry opportunity
Financial analysis: calculate breakeven (fixed costs / contribution margin per bottle) and estimate time to breakeven given realistic market share
Positioning strategy: use customer survey data to identify where 'other' products resonate and which beverage-type positioning (sports, leisure, etc.) offers the best opening
Risk assessment: evaluate market, competitive, cannibalization, and timing risks
Go/no-go recommendation: synthesize financials and positioning into a clear CEO recommendation

questions.prompt: What insights do you draw from Exhibit 1?
questions.guidance: Non-sparkling water is only 10% of the overall flavored water market, so the addressable segment is relatively small. Within non-sparkling, two competitors (Easy Drink at 18%, O2 at 12%) have meaningful but not dominant shares, while 70% is fragmented among 'others' — suggesting the client could realistically emerge as a third sizable player in a still-fragmented market.

questions.prompt: What is the potential size of the non-sparkling water market in number of bottles sold and in revenue?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask what units to use before calculating. Should correctly apply the 10% share to total gallons, convert gallons to bottles using the oz-per-gallon and oz-per-bottle figures, then apply the price per bottle.

math.setup: Total flavored water market = 8 million gallons/year. Non-sparkling share = 10%. Bottle size = 16 oz. 1 gallon = 64 oz. Price = $1/bottle.
steps: Bottles per gallon = 64 oz ÷ 16 oz = 4 bottles/gallon
math.answer: 3.2 million bottles sold per year; $3.2 million in annual revenue

questions.prompt: How long would it take the client to break even on the new product?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate contribution margin per bottle, derive bottles needed to cover fixed costs, then estimate realistic annual volume using a justified market share assumption. Should flag that 8 years is very long for the beverage industry and effectively calls the investment into question.

math.setup: Fixed/launch costs = $400,000. Variable cost = $0.90/bottle. Price = $1.00/bottle. Contribution margin = $0.10/bottle. Total non-sparkling market = 3.2 million bottles/year.
steps: 4 million bottles > entire annual market of 3.2 million bottles — will take more than one year
Market share assumption: as a major company with strong brand and distribution, likely to land between the two main competitors (12%–18%); use midpoint of ~15%
math.answer: Approximately 8 years to break even at ~15% market share; candidate should note this is extremely long for the beverage industry.

questions.prompt: If the client wanted to proceed with the product launch, how should they position the product in the market?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask how the two main competitors are currently positioned before answering. After reviewing the customer survey chart (Exhibit 2), should identify that the 'other' category has its largest share in the sports drink and leisure beverage segments, and recommend the client target one or both of those positioning spaces to maximize share opportunity.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks should the client consider when thinking about proceeding with this venture?

categories.name: Market / Demand risk
ideas: Flavored water may be a passing fad — customer preferences could shift quickly
Overall non-sparkling water market is small and may not grow

categories.name: Competitive risk
ideas: Incumbent competitors (Easy Drink, O2) may respond aggressively with price cuts or increased marketing
New entrants could further crowd the market

categories.name: Internal / Cannibalization risk
ideas: Client may already sell similar products that would be cannibalized by the new launch
Diversion of manufacturing and distribution capacity from higher-margin products

categories.name: Financial / Timing risk
ideas: Breakeven of ~8 years is unreasonably long for the fast-moving beverage industry
Trends and consumer preferences may change before the investment is recouped

recommendation: This is a questionable investment at best — the breakeven period of approximately 8 years is far too long to be reasonable in the beverage industry, where trends shift rapidly

If the client nonetheless decides to launch, they should leverage their strong brand name and owned distribution network to position the product as a sports drink or leisure beverage, where the 'other' category has its largest relative market share
risks: Flavored water trends are volatile; the window to recoup the investment may close before breakeven
Competitors may respond aggressively, compressing margins or market share below the assumed 15%
Cannibalization of existing client products could reduce net incremental gain
The long payback period diverts resources from potentially higher-return opportunities
next_steps: Conduct deeper consumer research to assess whether the sports/leisure positioning is defensible and differentiated
Evaluate whether launch costs could be reduced to bring breakeven within a more acceptable 3–5 year window
Analyze the client's existing portfolio for cannibalization exposure before committing to launch
